members.name: Andrew F. Mathieson
members.bioHtml:
Andy is the founder and managing member of Fairview Capital Investment Management, LLC. Prior to starting Fairview, Andy was a principal at Ashfield & Co, Inc. He earned his undergraduate degree from Yale University in 1978, and his MBA from Stanford University in 1984.

Andy is on the Board of Dominican University in San Rafael and works in an advisory capacity for the Santa Lucia Conservancy. Andy also serves on the board of DiCon Fiberoptics, a private Richmond, California-based manufacturer of passive optical components, integrated modules and test instruments.

Andy previously has served on the Boards of Guide Dogs for the Blind, The Branson School, and the Bay Area Discovery Museum. He has also been active in the community as a youth sports coach (soccer and softball), a mentor, and a fundraiser for many Marin-based causes.

members.name: P. Renae Branscum
members.teaser: Making sure clients always have support.
members.bioHtml: Renae became a member of the client service and operations team after having been the executive assistant to Fairview’s founder. Previously, she was a senior administrative assistant for KPMG LLP, the U.S. audit, tax and advisory services firm. Earlier she was an executive assistant at StarMine and executive assistant to the president at Triplex, an infoUSA Company. Renae also has experience as a human resources administrator and head bookkeeper. To expand the in-office support to Fairview clients, Renae became a licensed notary public in July, 2011.

members.name: Peter Mathieson
members.teaser: A long view on wealth and advice.
members.bioHtml:
Peter joined the firm in 2012 to establish the Pittsburgh office. Previously, he was the President and a principal shareholder of Guyasuta Investment Advisors, an asset management firm in Pittsburgh that he co-founded in 1994. He earned a BA in Economics from Bucknell University in 1983.

Peter currently sits on the Board of Directors of the Museum of The Rockies, the One Valley Community Foundation, Big Sky Youth Empowerment, and the Arts Council of Big Sky. Peter also serves on the investment committee of the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust and is an emeritus board member of the Pittsburgh Foundation.
